result: “Lazy training” — fast convergence with parameters barely moving — is not special to wide networks but a consequence of scale: multiplying the model by α (or the initialization of a homogeneous net) makes gradient descent follow the linearized model, with ‖w − w₀‖ = O(1/α) and distance to the linear path O(1/α²); experiments show this regime generalizes worse.
result_plain: Lazy training comes from scaling: training follows the linearization (O(1/α) motion); it hurts performance in practice.
